B: Hello! Hi, sorry, can you see me? My camera has gone very dark suddenly.
A: Yeah, I can see you, you're fine. A bit shadowy, but fine. I'm Gemma, Maidstone.
B: Oh, thank goodness. Sorry. I'm Nadeesha, in Cardiff. I'm a senior procurement officer for an NHS health board, so tenders, supplier contracts, that sort of thing.
A: Oh, very nice. I'm a branch manager, lettings and estates, team of five. So we're both sort of negotiating all day, aren't we?
B: Exactly, actually! It's all negotiating. The suppliers always say the price is fixed, and it's never fixed.
A: Same with landlords. They all think their flat's worth two hundred more than it is. Mind you, sometimes I tell them it is, if I think I can get it. Don't tell anyone.
B: I won't, I won't! Erm, I loved your kitchen in the photo, by the way. Very sleek, the grey.
A: Aw, thank you. I was going to say the same about yours, that big tea plantation picture. Is that Sri Lanka?
B: Yes, the hill country, near where my family are, in Kandy. We go back every other year for a month.
A: Lovely. We've been wanting a new kitchen, actually, a proper island, but Dean says we can't really justify it yet. Which, fair, but still.
B: Oh, I have the same with my husband, but with the car. I want a bigger one, an SUV, and Dilan says the Corolla is fine. It's not fine! With the school run and my mother visiting, it's not fine.
A: Men, honestly. Do they not see what we do? This morning I sat on the A20 for forty minutes, and he's telling me the car's fine.
B: Yes! Exactly.
A: Do you do holidays as well, apart from Sri Lanka?
B: City breaks, mostly. Lisbon last year, Barcelona before. And we stopped in Dubai on the way home once, which was, sorry, very luxurious. A really nice hotel.
A: Ooh. I'm all-inclusive, me. Turkey, Greece, pool, cocktail, done. I always try to get the upgrade. But I hate the flying bit, I check the passports about six times.
B: Oh my god, me too. I print everything. Dilan laughs at me, he says it's all on the phone, and I say, what if the phone dies?
A: Exactly! What if it dies! I've got Amsterdam coming up for my friend's fortieth, girls' weekend, and I'm already stressing. I'm meant to be booking the table for the Saturday night and nowhere's got anything for eight people.
B: That's a lot of pressure, actually, being the one who books.
A: It is. If it's rubbish, it's my fault. Sorry, am I going on?
B: No, no, not at all. I'm the same at work, if the contract goes wrong, it's me. Is that, sorry, is that what you were asking?
A: Ha, I wasn't really asking anything. What do you do to wind down, then?
B: Korean dramas. Terrible, I watch three episodes and it's one o'clock. And I have a new air fryer, I'm obsessed. I put everything in it.
A: Air fryer chicken is basically my whole week. And Love Island, which is a load of rubbish, but I still watch it.
B: I haven't watched that, actually. Is it good?
A: No! But you can't stop. You'd have to start from the...
